results.evidence: Retry found no page that assigns a commitment grade (II, III or IV) to Ottohorn's east ridge / southeast route. Accounts describe it only by class: class III in the 1961 first-ascent record, class 4 in later enchainment accounts, and 'class 3, one of the few non-fifth-class Southern Picket summits' in a traverse report. The row's other fields (rope_note and experienceLevel say III-IV; commitment III) do not agree well enough to settle it internally. Would settle: a current guidebook or route page that states the commitment grade for this line.

results.fact: Approach line at the cairn (Terror Basin path vs Terror Creek)
results.evidence: Retry shows there are TWO real lines, and the row mixes them. One party bound for the Chopping Block wrote that where the Terror Basin approach turns sharply uphill they continued straight and waded Terror Creek (calf-deep, cairn on the far bank), which matches pro_tips[1] and waypoints[1-3]; another party crossed Terror Creek near 2,040-2,100 ft on the way to Chopping Block camp. The approach text's profile (traverse ~3,200 ft, talus ~4,000, rock band ~4,800, gully to ~5,200, heather to the ~6,200 ft Barrier notch) is the Terror Basin trail, which turns uphill at the cairn and does not ford Terror Creek, confirmed by a separate Terror Basin trip report and the Terror Basin trail descriptions. Neither line is wrong, so the fix is an owner choice of which line this route presents (then rewrite the approach or re-sequence waypoints/pro tip to that one line), not a single wrong value.

results.fact: Rappels on the south side of the Otto-Himmel col
results.evidence: Sources still disagree: a traverse description says the south side of the col is 'a bit more friendly' and the technical part is over once in Crescent Creek Basin (consistent with descent_text / rappels '0'), while the 2017 first-ascent party rappelled above a giant chockstone in the Otto-Himmel gully to Crescent Creek Basin and an August traverse party used three rappel anchors on the south side. Likely snow-dependent. Would settle: a second late-season account of descending the south side, or wording that frames rappels as conditions-dependent approved by the owner.

In the fresh snapshot the itinerary totals agree with the columns (gain 2,600 + 900 = 3,500 = gain_ft; loss 100 + 3,600 = 3,700 = loss_ft), because the day-1 correction was never applied. The underlying problem remains: day 1 gains 2,600 ft to Burgundy Col, while the Burgundy Col waypoint note says the col is 3,700 ft above the creek crossing and a route page states the trail climbs 3,700+ ft to the col. Raising day 1 would break agreement with gain_ft, and no source states a car-to-car gain for Pernod's South Face, so no patch. Would settle: a stated car-to-car gain for this route.

Retry found no second source: the only published grade for Pernod's original line remains one comment calling Pernod and Chablis moderate 5.5-5.7 and not sustained; the route database lists only the Direct West Face (5.10+) and South Face (5.9 A0) on Pernod, and the 1952 account gives no modern grade. The 5.8 / 5.9 (A0) pitch table and itinerary appear borrowed from the South Face. Would settle: any second route page or trip report grading the 1952 line.

Only the 1952 account describes this line's descent (rappels to the notch, then long rappels to the glacier below, no count); rappel_detail / rappel_count_note / rappels '3' describe the South Face's descent via Chablis' east-face line. No second source for the count or line was found on retry. Would settle: a modern trip report descending Pernod's original route.

No source gives a commitment grade for Pernod's original route; the 'easy day' phrasing comes from a single comment, and the 1952 account called it strenuous for its time. Nothing new found on retry. Would settle: a route page stating the commitment grade. (Separately, beta opens by crediting a guidebook, which the no-sources rule forbids.)

Fresh snapshot: itinerary gain 2,600 + 900 = 3,500 vs gain_ft 4,000, and loss 100 + 3,600 = 3,700 vs loss_ft 4,000. Day 1's 2,600 ft to Burgundy Col is also short of the 3,700+ ft a route page gives for the climb to the col. Would settle: a stated car-to-car gain/loss for Pernod's original route.
